key_insight: PoliVEM unifies multiple virtual element formulations for solid mechanics in one Python-driven framework with a shared C++17 core, common projections, and reusable assembly/solver infrastructure.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical, extensible platform for beams, elasticity, diffusion, and hyperelasticity on polygonal/polyhedral meshes, which can simplify developing and comparing advanced structural solvers.
method: Common VEM core with vertex/edge/face/cell DOF hierarchy
Shared energy/strain/L2 projection operators plus consistency-stabilization split
Composition-based architecture for mesh, material, element, assembler, and solver
evidence_signal: The paper validates the framework with polynomial reproduction, static-condensation recovery, patch tests, stiffness spectra, and comparisons against independent FEM results on polygonal and polyhedral meshes.
watch_item: High-order polynomial bases on anisotropic cells and memory usage from sparse direct factorization are identified as current limitations.
paper_title: PoliVEM: a Python-driven virtual element framework for computational solid mechanics
